sections.text:
The Box That Changed Trade

A. For most of recorded history, loading a ship looked much the same. Goods arrived at the quayside in sacks, barrels, bales and crates of every shape, and gangs of dockworkers carried, rolled or hoisted each item aboard, fitting it into the hold by hand. A single cargo ship in the early 1950s might hold tens of thousands of separate items, and loading or unloading it could take a week or more. Vessels often spent as many days tied up in port as they did at sea. The process was also costly in other ways: cargo was damaged by careless handling, and a share of it routinely disappeared into workers' pockets or onto passing lorries. For many goods, the expense of moving them across a few hundred metres of dock was a large fraction of the cost of the entire journey.

B. The notion of packing cargo into large, reusable boxes was not new. Railways in several countries had experimented with removable freight boxes in the early twentieth century, and some shipping lines used small steel crates, but these schemes stayed local and never spread widely. The decisive step came in 1956, when an American entrepreneur who had built his fortune running a trucking business bought a shipping company and had an old tanker converted to carry 58 detachable trailer bodies. It sailed from Newark to Houston, and the cost of loading it was a small fraction of the usual rate. What made the experiment important was not the box itself but the thinking behind it: the entrepreneur saw that the real business was not operating ships but moving goods, and that the ship was simply one link in a chain that also included lorries, trains and warehouses.

C. For the idea to work on a global scale, however, the boxes had to be identical. In the early years each company built containers to its own design, in lengths that varied from firm to firm, and a box belonging to one firm could not be lifted by another firm's cranes or fitted into its ships. Through the 1960s, engineers, manufacturers and government officials negotiated a common standard, and the International Organization for Standardization eventually settled on lengths of 20 and 40 feet, together with a uniform width and a strong steel fitting at each corner. These corner fittings, locked together with a simple twisting device, allow containers to be stacked many layers high and fastened securely to ships, rail wagons and lorry trailers. Standardisation also produced a new unit of measurement, the twenty-foot equivalent unit, or TEU. Above all, it meant that goods could be sealed inside a box at a factory and not handled again until they reached their final destination.

D. The new system transformed the geography of ports. A container terminal needs deep water for large ships, giant cranes and, above all, vast areas of flat land on which thousands of boxes can be stacked and sorted. Old harbours in the hearts of cities, squeezed between narrow streets and ageing warehouses, had no room to expand, and trade moved to new sites. In New York, activity drained away from the piers of Manhattan and Brooklyn towards spacious terminals across the harbour in New Jersey; in Britain, London's historic docks closed one after another while the small port of Felixstowe grew into the country's busiest container port. The human cost was severe. The economic historian Wilhelmina Oduya, in her study of three European ports, found that dock employment fell by roughly two-thirds within fifteen years of each port opening its first container terminal.

E. Ships changed just as dramatically. The first purpose-built container ships carried a few hundred boxes; the largest vessels today carry more than 20,000 TEU. Because cranes can move a container every minute or two, a ship that once spent a week in port may now be turned around in a matter of hours. Lower costs per box encouraged shipping lines to build ever bigger vessels and to merge into a handful of giant companies. Yet the port economist Kenji Varela argues that the most important gain was not cheapness but predictability. When manufacturers could be confident that a consignment would arrive on a given day, he says, they could reduce the stocks they held in reserve and spread production across several countries, assembling products from parts made thousands of kilometres apart.

F. Economists still debate how much of the growth in world trade since the 1960s can be credited to the container, but some have argued that its effect was greater than that of many trade agreements. Its success has also created new weaknesses. Because global supply chains depend on boxes arriving exactly when expected, a single blocked canal or a shortage of empty containers can delay deliveries around the world for months. And because a sealed steel box looks the same whatever it holds, customs authorities can physically inspect only a small proportion of those passing through their ports, which makes the system attractive to smugglers. The plain metal container remains one of the least noticed inventions of the twentieth century, but few objects have done more to shape the world economy.
sections.title: The Box That Changed Trade

questions.evidence: Old harbours in the hearts of cities, squeezed between narrow streets and ageing warehouses, had no room to expand, and trade moved to new sites

explanation.uk: В абзаці C описано сталеві кутові фітинги, завдяки яким контейнери можна ставити один на одний і кріпити до суден, вагонів і причепів.

questions.prompt: a reference to cargo being stolen
questions.evidence: a share of it routinely disappeared into workers' pockets or onto passing lorries

explanation.ru: В абзаце A сказано, что часть груза регулярно "disappeared" в карманах рабочих или в грузовиках, то есть его воровали. В абзаце F упоминаются контрабандисты, но там речь идёт о сокрытии незаконных товаров, а не о краже груза.
explanation.uk: В абзаці A сказано, що частина вантажу регулярно "disappeared" у кишенях робітників або у вантажівках, тобто його крали. В абзаці F згадано контрабандистів, але там ідеться про приховування незаконних товарів, а не про крадіжку вантажу.

questions.prompt: an argument that reliability brought greater benefits than lower costs
questions.evidence: the most important gain was not cheapness but predictability

explanation.en: In paragraph E, Kenji Varela argues that predictability (reliable arrival times) mattered more than cheapness.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E Kenji Varela утверждает, что предсказуемость (надёжные сроки прибытия) была важнее дешевизны.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E Kenji Varela стверджує, що передбачуваність (надійні терміни прибуття) важила більше, ніж дешевизна.

sections.text:
Can We Rebuild the Reef?

A. Coral reefs occupy less than one percent of the sea floor, yet they shelter roughly a quarter of all known marine species, protect coastlines from waves and support fisheries and tourism on which hundreds of millions of people depend. Over recent decades, however, many reefs have lost a large share of their living coral, and in some regions the reef that divers see today is a grey, weed-covered skeleton of what existed a generation ago. Against this background, a growing number of projects aim not merely to protect what remains but to put coral back.

B. To understand why reefs are struggling, it helps to know that a coral is not a plant or a rock but a colony of small animals called polyps. Inside their tissues live microscopic algae which, through photosynthesis, supply the coral with most of its food and give it its colour. This partnership is sensitive to temperature. When the water stays even one or two degrees above its usual summer maximum for several weeks, the relationship breaks down and the coral expels its algae, turning white. Such bleached corals are not yet dead, and they can recover if conditions return to normal quickly; if the heat persists, however, they starve. Some species cope better than others, but few escape entirely. As oceans have warmed, mass bleaching events that were once rare have become far more frequent, leaving less time for recovery between them.

C. Heat is not the only problem. As seawater absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, it becomes more acidic, which makes it harder for corals to build their limestone skeletons. Closer to shore, soil and fertiliser washed off farmland cloud the water and encourage the growth of seaweed, while overfishing removes the grazing fish that would normally keep that seaweed in check. Outbreaks of disease, which appear to spread more easily among stressed colonies, add a further threat. A reef weakened by these local pressures is often less able to survive a heatwave.

D. The most common restoration approach is sometimes called coral gardening. Small pieces are snipped from healthy colonies and hung on underwater frames or ropes, where they grow, protected from predators, until they are large enough to be fixed onto a damaged reef. A refinement of this technique involves cutting certain slow-growing corals into tiny fragments; because the wounded edges heal rapidly, these pieces can spread far faster than an intact colony. Other teams collect the eggs and sperm that corals release during annual spawning events, raise the larvae in tanks and then release them over degraded areas, an approach that can, in principle, cover much larger areas. Most nurseries are run by small organisations that rely heavily on volunteer divers.

E. How well does any of this work? A long-term survey led by marine ecologist Talia Gunawardena followed transplanted corals at forty sites for five years. Her team found that the method used mattered less than the place chosen: where the water was clear and herbivorous fish were plentiful, most transplants survived, whereas at sites polluted by run-off, the majority had died by the third year. In Gunawardena's view, restoration cannot succeed unless the local causes of decline are dealt with first. Fisheries researcher Sione Lautaha reached a related conclusion in a village-run project in the Pacific. Survival improved markedly, he reported, once local fishers helped choose sites, because they knew which spots were sheltered from strong currents. He also noted that the villagers who tended the nurseries became more willing to respect fishing restrictions nearby.

F. A more ambitious idea is to give corals a better chance against warming itself. Geneticist Beatriz Quintanilla has crossed corals from naturally hot lagoons with those from cooler waters, and in her laboratory trials some offspring withstood temperatures that bleached their cooler-water parents. She warns, though, that these heat-tolerant corals grew noticeably more slowly, and that nobody yet knows whether such traits will remain useful if seas continue to warm. Her next step is to test the crossbred corals on an open reef, where conditions are far less predictable than in a tank.

G. Cost and scale remain the hardest obstacles. Economist Lars Edvardsen estimated that gardening projects typically spend tens of thousands of dollars to restore a single hectare, while the reefs being damaged each year are measured in thousands of square kilometres. He argues that, in many places, the same money would achieve more if spent on reducing farm run-off or enforcing fishing limits. Few restoration practitioners would disagree that their work cannot replace cuts in greenhouse gas emissions. What restoration can do is buy time: maintaining breeding populations, keeping key sites alive for tourism and coastal protection, and preserving genetic diversity that may prove valuable later. Restoration, in other words, is best seen not as a cure but as one part of a much broader effort, and its success will ultimately depend on decisions taken far from any reef.
sections.title: Can We Rebuild the Reef?

questions.prompt: Coral reefs cover around a quarter of the ocean floor.
questions.evidence: occupy less than one percent of the sea floor

explanation.en: Paragraph A says reefs cover less than one percent of the sea floor. The 'quarter' in the passage refers to the share of marine species reefs shelter, not the area they cover.
explanation.ru: В абзаце A сказано, что рифы занимают меньше одного процента морского дна. Слово "quarter" в тексте относится к доле морских видов, которым рифы дают убежище, а не к их площади.
explanation.uk: В абзаці A сказано, що рифи займають менше ніж один відсоток морського дна. Слово "quarter" у тексті стосується частки морських видів, яким рифи дають притулок, а не їхньої площі.

questions.prompt: Corals obtain most of their nutrition from the algae living inside them.
questions.evidence: supply the coral with most of its food

explanation.en: Paragraph B says the algae inside the coral's tissues supply it with most of its food, which is the same idea as 'most of their nutrition'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B говорится, что водоросли в тканях коралла дают ему большую часть пищи. Это та же мысль, что и "most of their nutrition".
explanation.uk: В абзаці B ідеться про те, що водорості в тканинах корала дають йому більшу частину їжі. Це та сама думка, що й "most of their nutrition".

questions.prompt: Bleached corals always die within a few weeks.
questions.evidence: Such bleached corals are not yet dead, and they can recover if conditions return to normal quickly

explanation.en: Paragraph B says bleached corals are not yet dead and can recover if conditions improve quickly. They die only if the heat continues, so 'always die' contradicts the passage.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B сказано, что обесцвеченные кораллы ещё не мертвы и могут восстановиться, если условия быстро улучшатся. Они погибают, только если жара продолжается, поэтому "always die" противоречит тексту.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що знебарвлені корали ще не мертві й можуть відновитися, якщо умови швидко покращаться. Вони гинуть, лише якщо спека триває, тому "always die" суперечить тексту.

questions.prompt: Fertiliser washed off farmland is now a greater threat to reefs than ocean acidification.

explanation.en: Paragraph C describes both acidification and farm run-off as problems, but it never compares how serious they are. The passage does not say which threat is greater.
explanation.ru: Абзац C описывает как проблемы и закисление океана, и сток с ферм, но нигде не сравнивает, насколько они серьёзны. В тексте не сказано, какая угроза больше.
explanation.uk: Абзац C описує як проблеми і закиснення океану, і стік із ферм, але ніде не порівнює, наскільки вони серйозні. У тексті не сказано, яка загроза більша.

questions.prompt: Coral pieces growing in nurseries are kept safe from animals that would eat them.
questions.evidence: where they grow, protected from predators

explanation.en: Paragraph D says the pieces grow on frames or ropes 'protected from predators', meaning they are kept safe from animals that would eat them.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D сказано, что фрагменты растут на рамах или верёвках "protected from predators", то есть защищены от животных, которые могли бы их съесть.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що фрагменти ростуть на рамах або мотузках "protected from predators", тобто захищені від тварин, які могли б їх з'їсти.

questions.prompt: Releasing coral larvae over damaged areas has proved more successful than coral gardening.

explanation.en: Paragraph D says the larvae method can 'in principle' cover larger areas, but it says nothing about whether it has actually worked better than gardening. Its success is left open.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D говорится, что метод с личинками "in principle" может охватывать большие площади, но ничего не сказано о том, действительно ли он оказался эффективнее выращивания фрагментов («садоводства»). Вопрос о его успехе остаётся открытым.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D ідеться про те, що метод із личинками "in principle" може охоплювати більші площі, але нічого не сказано про те, чи справді він виявився ефективнішим за вирощування фрагментів («садівництво»). Питання про його успіх залишається відкритим.

questions.prompt: Taking part in restoration work can make local people more supportive of protecting fish stocks.
questions.evidence: the villagers who tended the nurseries became more willing to respect fishing restrictions nearby

explanation.en: In paragraph E, Lautaha noticed that villagers who looked after the nurseries became more willing to respect fishing rules, which shows a change in their attitude.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E Lautaha заметил, что жители деревни, ухаживавшие за питомниками, стали охотнее соблюдать правила рыболовства. Это показывает, что их отношение изменилось.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E Lautaha помітив, що мешканці села, які доглядали за розсадниками, стали охочіше дотримуватися правил рибальства. Це свідчить про зміну їхнього ставлення.

questions.prompt: Corals that are better able to survive heat may pay for it by growing more slowly.
questions.evidence: these heat-tolerant corals grew noticeably more slowly

explanation.en: Paragraph F reports Quintanilla's warning that her heat-tolerant corals grew noticeably more slowly, a cost of their heat resistance.
explanation.ru: В абзаце F приводится предупреждение Quintanilla: её теплоустойчивые кораллы росли заметно медленнее. Это плата за их устойчивость к жаре.
explanation.uk: В абзаці F наведено застереження Quintanilla: її теплостійкі корали росли помітно повільніше. Це ціна їхньої стійкості до спеки.

questions.prompt: In some places, funds could be better used on tackling sources of damage than on replanting coral.
questions.evidence: the same money would achieve more if spent on reducing farm run-off or enforcing fishing limits

explanation.en: Paragraph G says Edvardsen argues the same money would achieve more if spent on cutting run-off or enforcing fishing limits. Gunawardena also stresses local causes, but she does not talk about money.
explanation.ru: В абзаце G сказано, что, по мнению Edvardsen, те же деньги принесли бы больше пользы, если бы их потратили на сокращение стока или на контроль за соблюдением ограничений на вылов. Gunawardena тоже подчёркивает роль местных причин, но о деньгах она не говорит.
explanation.uk: В абзаці G сказано, що, на думку Edvardsen, ті самі гроші дали б більше користі, якби їх витратили на скорочення стоку або на контроль за дотриманням обмежень на вилов. Gunawardena теж наголошує на місцевих причинах, але про гроші вона не говорить.

questions.prompt: Transplanted corals are unlikely to last unless the local reasons for reef decline are addressed first.
questions.evidence: restoration cannot succeed unless the local causes of decline are dealt with first

explanation.en: Paragraph E gives Gunawardena's view that restoration cannot succeed unless local causes of decline are dealt with first. Edvardsen talks about spending money differently, not about restoration failing.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E приводится мнение Gunawardena: восстановление не может быть успешным, пока не устранены местные причины деградации рифов. Edvardsen говорит о том, что деньги лучше тратить иначе, а не о провале восстановления.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E наведено думку Gunawardena: відновлення не може бути успішним, доки не усунуто місцеві причини деградації рифів. Edvardsen говорить про те, що гроші краще витрачати інакше, а не про провал відновлення.

groups.instruction: Look at the following statements and the list of researchers below. Match each statement with the correct researcher, A, B, C or D. NB You may use any letter more than once.

questions.prompt: A coral is in fact a colony of tiny animals, which are known as ______, and these rely on algae inside them for food.
questions.evidence: a colony of small animals called polyps

explanation.en: Paragraph B explains that a coral is a colony of small animals called polyps.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B объясняется, что коралл — это колония мелких животных, которых называют "polyps" (полипы).
explanation.uk: В абзаці B пояснюється, що корал — це колонія дрібних тварин, яких називають "polyps" (поліпи).

questions.prompt: As the ocean takes in carbon dioxide and becomes more acidic, corals find it more difficult to form their ______.
questions.evidence: makes it harder for corals to build their limestone skeletons

explanation.en: Paragraph C says acidic water makes it harder for corals to build their limestone skeletons; 'form' restates 'build'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что в закисленной воде кораллам труднее строить свои известковые скелеты ("limestone skeletons"); "form" здесь перефразирует "build".
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що в закисленій воді коралам важче будувати свої вапнякові скелети ("limestone skeletons"); "form" тут перефразовує "build".

questions.prompt: Near the coast, overfishing removes the fish that normally control the growth of ______.
questions.evidence: the grazing fish that would normally keep that seaweed in check

explanation.en: Paragraph C says overfishing removes grazing fish that keep seaweed in check, which means they control its growth.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C говорится, что перелов уничтожает растительноядных рыб ("grazing fish"), которые "keep seaweed in check", то есть сдерживают рост водорослей.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C ідеться про те, що надмірний вилов знищує рослиноїдних риб ("grazing fish"), які "keep seaweed in check", тобто стримують ріст водоростей.

groups.instruction: Complete the summary below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

sections.text:
Why the Pencil Still Matters

A. Walk into almost any secondary classroom today and you are likely to see more screens than exercise books. Pupils draft essays on laptops, submit homework through online platforms and, increasingly, sit examinations on computers. Against this background, a question that would once have seemed absurd is now asked seriously by parents and policymakers alike: why should children spend hundreds of hours learning to form letters with a pen when they will spend most of their adult lives typing? It is a fair question, and it deserves a better answer than nostalgia. My own view is that handwriting should remain a core part of early education, but for reasons that have little to do with tradition.

B. The case against handwriting is not foolish. Ruth Calloway, who advises schools on digital learning, points out that typing is faster for most fluent users, produces text that is easy to edit and share, and removes a barrier for children whose control of a pencil develops slowly. In her experience, some pupils who struggle to write legibly become far more willing to express themselves once they are allowed a keyboard. She argues that the time spent drilling joined-up letters could be better used teaching pupils to touch-type, search for information and judge the reliability of what they find online. These are genuine skills, and any curriculum that ignores them is failing its students. Calloway is no enemy of the pen; she simply believes its place in the timetable has become too large.

C. Yet her argument rests on an assumption that handwriting is simply a slower way of recording words. There is growing evidence that it is also a way of learning them. Researchers have found that when young children practise forming letters by hand, they tend to recognise those letters more readily afterwards than children who learn them by pressing keys. The likely explanation is that drawing a letter forces the learner to attend to its shape, stroke by stroke, whereas a key produces an identical, finished symbol whatever the hand does. In other words, the effort that makes handwriting slow may be precisely what makes it valuable.

D. A study by the psychologist Annelise Moreau points in a similar direction for older pupils. She asked two groups of fourteen-year-olds to take notes during a short lecture, one group writing by hand and the other using laptops. When tested a week later, the two groups remembered roughly the same number of facts, but the handwriting group performed noticeably better on questions that required them to explain ideas in their own words. Moreau suggests that because people writing by hand cannot keep pace with a speaker, they are obliged to summarise, and summarising requires them to process meaning rather than merely transcribe sound. She is careful to describe her results as preliminary, and her sample was small. Nonetheless, the study fits a pattern that many teachers have long observed informally.

E. One such teacher is Daniyar Petrossian, head of a primary school that reintroduced daily handwriting practice after several years of relying mainly on tablets. He had noticed, he says, that pupils' spelling was growing weaker, partly because automatic correction software fixed their errors before the children were even aware of them. After the change, spelling scores rose steadily over two years, although Petrossian admits that the school also hired an extra reading specialist during the same period, so he cannot be sure which change mattered more. His frankness is welcome. Debates about education are too often settled by anecdote presented as proof, and claims for handwriting deserve the same scrutiny as claims for any new technology.

F. None of this means schools should return to the classrooms of a century ago, where children were punished for untidy loops and every pupil was expected to produce the same elegant script. That approach confused handwriting with penmanship, treating appearance as the goal rather than fluency. What matters is that a child can write quickly and legibly enough that the physical act no longer absorbs their attention, leaving the mind free to concentrate on ideas. Once that point is reached, the decorative extras of traditional cursive add little, and the time saved can reasonably be given to typing.

G. There is also a practical argument that is rarely heard. Technology fails: batteries run flat, networks go down, and examinations in many subjects still require written answers. Teachers who have supervised a room of pupils whose laptops have suddenly lost power will know how quickly a lesson can collapse. A pupil who has never developed a comfortable, reasonably fast hand is at a disadvantage in all of these situations, through no fault of their own.

H. The real choice, then, is not between pen and keyboard but about sequence and balance. Children should learn to write by hand first, because it appears to support the early recognition of letters and words, and they should learn to type well later, because the adult world demands it. Treating the two as rivals has produced a debate that generates more heat than light. Treating them as partners would give children the best of both, and that, rather than a nostalgic defence of the fountain pen, is the case worth making.
sections.title: Why the Pencil Still Matters

questions.prompt: The question of whether children still need to learn handwriting does not deserve serious consideration.
questions.evidence: It is a fair question, and it deserves a better answer than nostalgia.

explanation.en: In paragraph A the writer says the question once seemed absurd but now calls it 'a fair question' that deserves a proper answer. This is the opposite of the statement.
explanation.ru: В абзаце A автор говорит, что когда-то этот вопрос казался абсурдным, но теперь называет его «a fair question», который заслуживает серьёзного ответа. Это противоположно утверждению.
explanation.uk: В абзаці A автор каже, що колись це питання здавалося абсурдним, але тепер називає його «a fair question», яке заслуговує на належну відповідь. Це протилежне твердженню.

questions.prompt: Schools that do not teach typing and online research skills are letting their pupils down.
questions.evidence: These are genuine skills, and any curriculum that ignores them is failing its students.

explanation.en: In paragraph B the writer agrees with Calloway that these are genuine skills and says a curriculum that ignores them is 'failing its students', which means letting them down.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B автор соглашается с Calloway, что это настоящие навыки, и говорит, что учебная программа, которая их игнорирует, «failing its students», то есть подводит учеников.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B автор погоджується з Calloway, що це справжні навички, і каже, що навчальна програма, яка їх ігнорує, «failing its students», тобто підводить учнів.

questions.prompt: Most children find touch-typing harder to learn than handwriting.

explanation.en: Paragraph B mentions teaching pupils to touch-type, and paragraph H says children should learn to type later. The writer never compares how difficult the two skills are to learn.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B упоминается обучение учеников слепой печати, а в абзаце H говорится, что детям стоит учиться печатать позже. Но автор нигде не сравнивает, насколько трудно освоить эти два навыка.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B згадується навчання учнів сліпого друку, а в абзаці H сказано, що дітям варто вчитися друкувати пізніше. Але автор ніде не порівнює, наскільки важко опанувати ці дві навички.

questions.prompt: Petrossian was right to admit that something else might explain the improvement in spelling.
questions.evidence: His frankness is welcome.

explanation.en: In paragraph E Petrossian admits that hiring a reading specialist may also have helped. The writer calls this frankness 'welcome', so the writer approves of his honesty.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E Petrossian признаёт, что помочь мог и нанятый специалист по чтению. Автор называет такую откровенность «welcome», значит, он одобряет честность Petrossian.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E Petrossian визнає, що допомогти міг і найнятий фахівець із читання. Автор називає таку відвертість «welcome», отже, він схвалює чесність Petrossian.

questions.prompt: Children should be expected to produce neat, uniform handwriting.
questions.evidence: That approach confused handwriting with penmanship, treating appearance as the goal rather than fluency.

explanation.en: In paragraph F the writer criticises old classrooms where every pupil had to produce the same elegant script, saying they wrongly made appearance the goal. The writer cares about speed and legibility, not uniform neatness.
explanation.ru: В абзаце F автор критикует старые классы, где каждый ученик должен был выводить одинаковый красивый почерк, и говорит, что там ошибочно делали целью внешний вид. Для автора важны скорость и разборчивость, а не единообразная аккуратность.
explanation.uk: В абзаці F автор критикує старі класи, де кожен учень мусив виводити однаковий гарний почерк, і каже, що там помилково робили метою зовнішній вигляд. Для автора важливі швидкість і розбірливість, а не однакова охайність.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in the passage? Write YES if the statement agrees with the views of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the views of the writer, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.

options.text: become more willing to express themselves when allowed to type.
helps them to recognise those letters more easily afterwards.
remembered a similar number of facts to the other group.
are forced to condense what they hear into a summary.
stopped children from noticing their own spelling errors.
treated how writing looks as more important than how fluently it flows.
gave better explanations of the ideas in their own words.
was the main cause of the rise in spelling scores.

questions.prompt: Ruth Calloway has found that some pupils who struggle to write legibly
questions.evidence: some pupils who struggle to write legibly become far more willing to express themselves once they are allowed a keyboard

explanation.en: Paragraph B says that, in Calloway's experience, these pupils express themselves more readily once they can use a keyboard, which means typing.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B говорится, что, по опыту Calloway, эти ученики охотнее выражают свои мысли, когда могут пользоваться клавиатурой («keyboard»), то есть печатать.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що, з досвіду Calloway, ці учні охочіше висловлюють свої думки, коли можуть користуватися клавіатурою («keyboard»), тобто друкувати.

questions.prompt: Research suggests that, for young children, practising letter shapes by hand
questions.evidence: they tend to recognise those letters more readily afterwards than children who learn them by pressing keys

explanation.en: Paragraph C reports that children who form letters by hand recognise them more readily later than children who learn them by pressing keys.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сообщается, что дети, которые выводят буквы от руки, потом узнают их легче, чем дети, которые учат буквы, нажимая на клавиши.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C повідомляється, що діти, які виводять літери від руки, згодом упізнають їх легше, ніж діти, які вчать літери, натискаючи на клавіші.

questions.prompt: In Annelise Moreau's study, the pupils who used laptops
questions.evidence: the two groups remembered roughly the same number of facts

explanation.en: Paragraph D says both groups remembered roughly the same number of facts. It was the handwriting group, not the laptop group, that explained ideas better, so the ending about better explanations is wrong.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D говорится, что обе группы запомнили примерно одинаковое количество фактов. Лучше объясняли идеи те, кто писал от руки, а не те, кто работал на ноутбуках, поэтому окончание про более удачные объяснения неверно.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що обидві групи запам'ятали приблизно однакову кількість фактів. Краще пояснювали ідеї ті, хто писав від руки, а не ті, хто працював на ноутбуках, тому закінчення про кращі пояснення неправильне.

questions.prompt: Moreau believes that people taking notes by hand
questions.evidence: cannot keep pace with a speaker, they are obliged to summarise

explanation.en: In paragraph D Moreau suggests that hand writers cannot keep up with the speaker, so they have to summarise what they hear.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D Moreau предполагает, что пишущие от руки не успевают за говорящим, поэтому им приходится кратко излагать услышанное своими словами.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D Moreau припускає, що ті, хто пише від руки, не встигають за мовцем, тому їм доводиться стисло переказувати почуте своїми словами.

questions.prompt: Daniyar Petrossian thinks that automatic correction software
questions.evidence: automatic correction software fixed their errors before the children were even aware of them

explanation.en: Paragraph E says the software corrected mistakes before children knew they had made them. The ending about the main cause of rising scores is wrong because Petrossian says he cannot be sure what caused the improvement.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E говорится, что программа исправляла ошибки ещё до того, как дети понимали, что их допустили. Окончание про главную причину роста результатов неверно, потому что Petrossian говорит, что не может точно знать, чем вызвано улучшение.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E сказано, що програма виправляла помилки ще до того, як діти усвідомлювали, що їх зробили. Закінчення про головну причину зростання результатів неправильне, бо Petrossian каже, що не може напевно знати, що спричинило покращення.

groups.instruction: Complete each sentence with the correct ending, A–H, from the box below. There are more endings than sentences, so you will not use them all.

questions.prompt: Calloway believes the hours used for practising ______ would be better spent on skills such as typing.
questions.evidence: the time spent drilling joined-up letters could be better used teaching pupils to touch-type

explanation.en: Paragraph B says Calloway thinks time spent 'drilling joined-up letters' could be better used for typing and other digital skills.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B говорится, что, по мнению Calloway, время, которое уходит на «drilling joined-up letters», лучше было бы потратить на обучение печати («typing») и другим цифровым навыкам («digital skills»).
explanation.uk: В абзаці B сказано, що, на думку Calloway, час, який іде на «drilling joined-up letters», краще було б витратити на навчання друку («typing») та інших цифрових навичок («digital skills»).

questions.prompt: Whatever movement the hand makes, pressing a key results in the same ______.
questions.evidence: a key produces an identical, finished symbol whatever the hand does

explanation.en: Paragraph C explains that a key always produces an identical, finished symbol, unlike drawing a letter stroke by stroke.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C объясняется, что клавиша всегда даёт одинаковый («identical») готовый символ, в отличие от буквы, которую рисуют штрих за штрихом.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C пояснюється, що клавіша завжди дає однаковий («identical») готовий символ, на відміну від літери, яку малюють штрих за штрихом.

questions.prompt: Moreau acknowledges that her sample was small and calls her results ______.
questions.evidence: She is careful to describe her results as preliminary, and her sample was small.

explanation.en: Paragraph D says Moreau carefully describes her results as preliminary, meaning early and not yet certain.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D говорится, что Moreau осторожно называет свои результаты предварительными («preliminary»), то есть ранними и пока не окончательными.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що Moreau обережно називає свої результати попередніми («preliminary»), тобто ранніми й ще не остаточними.

questions.prompt: Before reintroducing daily handwriting practice, Petrossian's school had depended largely on ______.
questions.evidence: after several years of relying mainly on tablets

explanation.en: Paragraph E says the school had relied mainly on tablets for several years before bringing back handwriting practice.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E говорится, что несколько лет школа в основном полагалась на планшеты («tablets»), прежде чем вернуть занятия письмом от руки.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E сказано, що кілька років школа здебільшого покладалася на планшети («tablets»), перш ніж повернути заняття з письма від руки.
